components.note: 火 (fire) — cooked to mush, then rotten; also in 烧 burn, 灯 lamp.
兰 (lán) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 栏 lán and 拦 lán.

example.pinyin: Zhège píngguǒ làn le.
example.english: This apple has gone bad.
example.fact: 烂 covers both rotten food and soft-cooked food, a happy meaning in cooking: 炖烂 means stewed until tender. Colloquially it means lousy (烂人 for a bad person) and 烂尾楼 is an unfinished building abandoned halfway.

examples.pinyin: Zhè kuài ròu zhǔ làn le, hěn hǎochī.
examples.english: This meat is stewed until tender, and it's delicious.

examples.pinyin: Tā de shǒujī píngmù làn le.
examples.english: His phone screen is wrecked.

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
灬 (fire) — heat and burning, as in 热 hot, 点 dot, 照 shine. 然 first meant "to burn" (燃 rán adds 火 later); "so, naturally" is borrowed.
肰 (rán) gives the exact sound and shows up in 燃 rán.

example.hanzi: 快点出发,不然我们要迟到了。
example.pinyin: Kuài diǎn chūfā, bùrán wǒmen yào chídào le.
example.english: Let's leave quickly, or else we'll be late.
example.fact: 不然 literally means "not so" (不 "not" + 然 "so, thus") and sets up an unwanted alternative if a preceding suggestion is not followed — the same 然 that appears in 然后 ("then") and 突然 ("suddenly"), a character whose core sense of "in this manner" recurs across several common connectors.

examples.hanzi: 你要多穿点，不然会感冒。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào duō chuān diǎn, bùrán huì gǎnmào.
examples.english: Wear more, otherwise you'll catch a cold.

examples.pinyin: Bùrán, wǒmen míngtiān zài qù ba.
examples.english: Otherwise, let's go tomorrow.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement: 过, 进, 送, 迎 welcome; 邀 is to go out to meet and invite.
敫 (jiǎo) is the sound part, only a loose clue for yāo.
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and asking: 说, 谢, 谈; 请 is to ask politely.
青 (qīng) sounds like 请 (tone differs); same part in 清, 情, 晴, 精, 静.

example.hanzi: 我们邀请了很多朋友来参加聚会。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen yāoqǐngle hěn duō péngyou lái cānjiā jùhuì.
example.english: We invited a lot of friends to come to the party.
example.fact: 邀请 doubles two verbs that already independently mean roughly "to invite, request" — 邀 ("to invite, entreat") and 请 ("please, to request") — the same reinforcing two-near-synonym pattern behind 舞蹈 and 寻找 elsewhere in this set.

examples.hanzi: 谢谢你邀请我参加你的婚礼。
examples.pinyin: Xièxie nǐ yāoqǐng wǒ cānjiā nǐ de hūnlǐ.
examples.english: Thank you for inviting me to your wedding.

examples.hanzi: 我收到了一份生日邀请。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shōudàole yí fèn shēngrì yāoqǐng.
examples.english: I received a birthday invitation.

components.note: 尺 (chǐ, ruler) — the visible top part, as in 尺寸 size. 尽 simplifies 盡 and the shape does not explain 'use up'. Memory aid: measure it to the very end.
⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo, as in 笔, 等, 算: a hollow pipe.
官 (guān) is a close sound clue for guǎn; 官 also in 馆 guǎn and 棺 guān.

example.hanzi: 尽管天气很冷,他还是坚持出去跑步。
example.pinyin: Jǐnguǎn tiānqì hěn lěng, tā háishi jiānchí chūqù pǎobù.
example.english: Although the weather was very cold, he still insisted on going out for a run.
example.fact: 尽管 sets up a concessive clause that typically pairs with 还是 or 但是 later on ("尽管...,还是...") to mean "even though X, Y still happens" — the same paired-clause logic recurs throughout this batch's connectors, including the 既然...就... and 无论...都... constructions.

examples.hanzi: 尽管很累，他还是完成了工作。
examples.pinyin: Jǐnguǎn hěn lèi, tā háishi wánchéngle gōngzuò.
examples.english: Although he was tired, he still finished the work.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu wèntí jǐnguǎn wèn wǒ.
examples.english: If you have questions, feel free to ask me.

components.note: 女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 好.
且 (qiě) is a loose sound clue for jiě; 且 also sounds out 祖 zǔ, 租 zū and 助 zhù.
女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 好.
且 (qiě) is a loose sound clue for jiě; 且 also sounds out 祖 zǔ, 租 zū and 助 zhù.

example.pinyin: Wǒ jiějie zài Běijīng gōngzuò.
example.english: My older sister works in Beijing.
example.fact: Chinese kinship terms encode relative age in a way English doesn't bother to: 姐姐 can only mean an OLDER sister, and a younger one is a completely different word, 妹妹 — English "sister" covers both without distinction, so learners have to relearn the concept of "sister" as inherently ranked.

examples.pinyin: Jiějie bǐ wǒ dà liǎng suì.
examples.english: My older sister is two years older than me.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ hé jiějie yìqǐ qù guàngjiē.
examples.english: My older sister and I go shopping together.

components.note: 氵 (water radical, 三点水) — water and waves: 河, 海, 汤; 浪 is a wave.
良 (liáng) is a loose clue; also in 狼 láng, 朗 lǎng and 娘 niáng.
贝 (cowry shell, money) — money and trade: 财, 货, 买, 贵; 费 is a cost or fee.
弗 (fú) is close to fèi; same part in 沸 fèi.

example.hanzi: 别浪费时间,快点做作业。
example.pinyin: Bié làngfèi shíjiān, kuài diǎn zuò zuòyè.
example.english: Don't waste time, hurry and do your homework.
example.fact: 浪费 can take almost any resource as its object — time, money, food, talent, an opportunity — functioning much like English "waste." Its more colloquial cousin 白费 ("to expend in vain," as in 白费力气) narrows in specifically on effort spent with nothing gained, a slightly different shade of the same basic idea.

examples.pinyin: Búyào làngfèi shíwù.
examples.english: Don't waste food.

examples.hanzi: 坐在这儿等太浪费时间了。
examples.pinyin: Zuò zài zhèr děng tài làngfèi shíjiān le.
examples.english: Sitting here waiting is such a waste of time.

components.note: 多 (many) — two 夕 stacked, repeated again and again: so "many, much, more".
讠 (speech) — words, as in 说, 请, 诉: you thank someone with words.
射 (shè) is a loose sound clue for xiè; in 谢谢 the tone drops to neutral on the second.

example.pinyin: Duōxiè nǐ de bāngzhù.
example.english: Many thanks for your help.
example.fact: 多谢 literally reads as "many thanks" — 多 ("many") intensifying 谢 ("to thank") the same way 非常 intensifies adjectives elsewhere in this deck. In standard Mandarin it can feel a touch more formal than 谢谢; in Cantonese, the same two characters (read do1 ze6) are simply the everyday, default way to say "thank you."

examples.pinyin: Duōxiè nǐ de yāoqǐng!
examples.english: Many thanks for your invitation!

examples.pinyin: “Duōxiè!” “Bú kèqi.”
examples.english: "Thanks a lot!" "You're welcome."

components.note: 女 (woman) — a person kneeling with arms crossed; as a radical it heads many female and family words: 妈, 好, 姐.
朋 (friend) — oldest form shows two strings of cowrie shells (old money) side by side; they paired up and came to mean companions.
又 (hand) — two hands 又 stacked: hands joined in friendship.

example.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ de nǚpéngyou.
example.english: This is my girlfriend.
example.fact: 朋友 already means "friend" on its own; adding 女 ("female") narrows it specifically to a romantic girlfriend, the same modification pattern that gives 男朋友 (also in this batch) for "boyfriend." Because of that romantic narrowing, a plain female friend has to be called something else, like 女性朋友, to avoid the girlfriend implication.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu nǚpéngyou ma?
examples.english: Do you have a girlfriend?

examples.hanzi: 他的女朋友是一名老师。
examples.pinyin: Tā de nǚpéngyou shì yì míng lǎoshī.
examples.english: His girlfriend is a teacher.

components.note: 力 (strength) — effort and motion, as in 办, 助, 努. The part 云 stands in for 重 in the traditional 動, which was the sound clue.
牛 (ox) — cattle words like 牧 herd and 特 special; 物 first referred to livestock, then to things in general.
勿 (wù) sounds exactly like 物 — handy for recalling the pronunciation.

example.hanzi: 熊猫是一种很可爱的动物。
example.pinyin: Xióngmāo shì yì zhǒng hěn kě'ài de dòngwù.
example.english: The panda is a very cute kind of animal.
example.fact: 动物 is built from 动 ("to move") plus 物 ("thing, object") — quite transparent logic: "a moving thing." It forms a clean pair with 植物 ("plant," literally "a planted thing"), the basic two-way split Chinese uses to sort living things by whether they move on their own.

examples.pinyin: Dòngwùyuán lǐ yǒu hěn duō dòngwù.
examples.english: There are many animals in the zoo.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuì xǐhuan de dòngwù shì gǒu.
examples.english: My favorite animal is the dog.

components.note: 一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
半 (half) — 牛 (an ox) divided in two by 八: half. Seen in 一半 half, 半夜 midnight.

example.hanzi: 这块蛋糕的一半是我的。
example.pinyin: Zhè kuài dàngāo de yíbàn shì wǒ de.
example.english: Half of this cake is mine.
example.fact: 一半 is one of the few fraction expressions used constantly in everyday speech rather than saved for math class — a full fraction in Chinese normally follows the pattern X分之Y (三分之一, "a third"), but "half" skips that whole template because 半 already means "half" outright.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhǐ chīle yíbàn.
examples.english: I only ate half.

examples.pinyin: Yíbàn de xuésheng láizì guówài.
examples.english: Half of the students come from abroad.

components.note: 木 (tree) — 某 first named a sour tree fruit; now it means a certain, unnamed one. It sounds out 媒 méi, 煤 méi and 谋 móu.
人 (person) — the top part. 个 is the general measure word, as in 一个, 这个, 那个.
丨 (a vertical tally) — under 人, read as one tally mark per person: counting individuals one by one.

example.hanzi: 我好像在某个地方见过他。
example.pinyin: Wǒ hǎoxiàng zài mǒu ge dìfang jiànguò tā.
example.english: I feel like I've seen him somewhere before.
example.fact: 某 deliberately keeps a person, place, or thing vague — 某个地方 ("somewhere"), 某个人 ("someone"), 某天 ("one day") — acting as Mandarin's built-in "unspecified X" slot, much like English "a certain" or "some" placed before a noun without committing to details.

examples.hanzi: 他住在城市的某个地方。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhù zài chéngshì de mǒu ge dìfang.
examples.english: He lives somewhere in the city.

examples.hanzi: 某个星期六我们去爬山吧。
examples.pinyin: Mǒu ge xīngqīliù wǒmen qù páshān ba.
examples.english: Let's go hiking some Saturday.

components.note: 身 (body) — the body ducking away; also in 躺 lie down, 躬.
朵 (duǒ) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 垛 duò.

example.pinyin: Háizi duǒ zài mén hòumian.
example.english: The child is hiding behind the door.
example.fact: 躲 is to hide oneself or dodge, whereas 藏 (cáng) is to hide something. For hide-and-seek, people say 躲猫猫 or 捉迷藏. 躲避 is the formal "avoid", as in 躲避危险.

examples.pinyin: Kuài duǒkāi, chē lái le!
examples.english: Quick, get out of the way, a car is coming!

examples.hanzi: 下雨了，我们找个地方躲一下。
examples.pinyin: Xià yǔ le, wǒmen zhǎo gè dìfang duǒ yíxià.
examples.english: It's raining, so let's find somewhere to take shelter.

components.note: 力 (strength) — visible inside 为. Memory aid: putting strength 力 into doing something; 为 is 'to do, to act' and, in 因为, 为什么, 'because/for'.
為 (traditional) — often explained as a hand leading an elephant to work. 为 is a cursive simplification, so the picture is no longer visible.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 们; 何 was a person carrying a load (荷 hè).
可 (kě) is a close sound clue for hé; also in 河 hé, 歌 gē and 哥 gē.

example.pinyin: Tā wèihé chíchí bù huífù?
example.english: Why hasn't he replied for so long?
example.fact: 为何 is a more literary, formal cousin of the everyday 为什么 — 何 alone is a classical-Chinese question word for "what, which," so 为何 shows up far more in writing, news headlines, and formal speech, while 为什么 dominates ordinary conversation.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ wèihé bù zǎo shuō?
examples.english: Why didn't you say so earlier?

examples.pinyin: Tā wèihé rúcǐ shēngqì?
examples.english: Why is he so angry?

components.note: 要 (want, need) — oldest form shows hands at a waist: it meant "waist" (腰 yāo adds 月 flesh); "essential" followed.
幺 (tiny, a thread) — 么 looks like 幺 and was borrowed as a simplified form for the light particle in 什么, 怎么, 这么. The shape does not explain the meaning today.
厶 (loop) — the visible lower part, a small curl. Memory aid: a tiny stroke 丿 over a curl — a 'little something' you ask about: 什么 what?

example.pinyin: Yàome nǐ lái, yàome wǒ qù.
example.english: Either you come, or I go.
example.fact: 要么 almost always appears twice in a row as a paired construction — "要么...,要么..." ("either... or...") — laying out two alternatives, much like English "either...or." Using it only once, without a matching partner, reads as incomplete to a native speaker.

examples.hanzi: 周末要么看电影，要么去爬山。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò yàome kàn diànyǐng, yàome qù páshān.
examples.english: At the weekend, either we watch a movie or we go hiking.

examples.hanzi: 要么你先走，要么我们一起等。
examples.pinyin: Yàome nǐ xiān zǒu, yàome wǒmen yìqǐ děng.
examples.english: Either you go first, or we wait together.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之) — marks movement; 逼 is pressing someone in, as in 逼近 close in and 逼迫 force.
畐 (fú) — loose sound hint (bī vs fú); same part sits in 福 fú and 副 fù.

example.pinyin: Bié bī wǒ, wǒ xūyào shíjiān.
example.english: Don't pressure me, I need time.
example.fact: 逼 means to force or press someone, often 逼 + person + verb: 逼我做. The idea of pressing close survives in 逼近 (to close in on) and 逼真 (lifelike, "pressing close to the real thing"). 被逼无奈 means "forced with no choice".

examples.pinyin: Méiyǒu rén bī nǐ zuò zhè jiàn shì.
examples.english: Nobody is forcing you to do this.

examples.pinyin: Lǎobǎn tiāntiān bī wǒ jiābān.
examples.english: The boss pushes me to work overtime every day.

components.note: 欠 (yawn, lack) — a person with an open mouth yawning; now means to owe or lack, as in 欠钱 owe money. As radical it marks mouth actions like 吹, 歌.

example.pinyin: Wǒ qiàn nǐ yí dùn fàn.
example.english: I owe you a meal.
example.fact: 欠 means to owe, not just money: 欠钱 (owe money), 欠你一个人情 (owe you a favour). It also means to lack, as in 欠缺. As a radical 欠 marks mouth actions, e.g. 吹, 歌, 欢.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ hái qiàn tā liǎngbǎi kuài qián.
examples.english: I still owe him two hundred yuan.

examples.hanzi: 我最近欠觉，每天都很困。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuìjìn qiàn jiào, měitiān dōu hěn kùn.
examples.english: I've been short on sleep lately and feel sleepy every day.

components.note: 车 (cart, vehicle) — marks wheeled things, as in 转, 车, 较; 轮 is a wheel.
仑 (lún) gives the sound exactly: 轮 lún, also in 论 lùn and 伦 lún.

example.pinyin: Zìxíngchē de lúnzi huài le.
example.english: The bicycle's wheel is broken.
example.fact: 轮 is a wheel and also the idea of turns: 轮到你了 ("it's your turn"), 轮流 (take turns). It counts rounds or cycles, as in 第一轮 (the first round) and is also the measure word for the sun or moon: 一轮明月.

examples.pinyin: Xià yí gè jiù lúndào nǐ le.
examples.english: You're next.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen lúnliú zuò fàn.
examples.english: We take turns cooking.

components.note: 讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and language: 说 say, 请 ask, 读 read; testing often involves questions.
式 (shì) sounds exactly like 试 — a reliable sound clue.
囗 (enclosure) — boundaries and surroundings: 国 country, 园 garden, 回 return; 图 is a drawn plan of a region.

example.hanzi: 警方试图找到失踪的男孩。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng shìtú zhǎodào shīzōng de nánhái.
example.english: The police attempted to find the missing boy.
example.fact: 试图 leans formal and shows up constantly in news reports about an ongoing or failed effort. In everyday speech, Mandarin speakers reach instead for the plainer 想 ("want to") or 试着 ("try to"), saving 试图 for a more deliberate, often unsuccessful attempt.

examples.pinyin: Tā shìtú shuōfú bàba.
examples.english: He tried to persuade his dad.

examples.hanzi: 她试图打开那扇门，但是打不开。
examples.pinyin: Tā shìtú dǎkāi nà shàn mén, dànshì dǎ bu kāi.
examples.english: She tried to open that door, but it wouldn't open.

components.note: 又 (hand) — a hand pushing against a cliff 厂: turning back, opposite. Sound series: 饭 fàn, 板 bǎn, 版 bǎn, 返 fǎn.
广 (building, shelter) — the roof-and-wall frame, as in 店, 床, 度. Here it is mostly the outline of the old 應.
心 (heart) — hidden in the traditional 應, 'respond from the heart'; simplification dropped it. 应 is yīng (should) or yìng (respond).

example.hanzi: 他听到这个消息后,没有任何反应。
example.pinyin: Tā tīngdào zhège xiāoxi hòu, méiyǒu rènhé fǎnyìng.
example.english: He had no reaction at all after hearing this news.
example.fact: 反应 covers both a person's emotional or physical reaction and a chemical reaction (化学反应) with the exact same word — English sometimes reaches for different terms across those registers, but Mandarin's 反应 spans both without needing a separate word.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de fǎnyìng zhēn kuài.
examples.english: Your reaction is really quick.

examples.hanzi: 我对这种药有反应，吃了就不舒服。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ duì zhè zhǒng yào yǒu fǎnyìng, chīle jiù bù shūfu.
examples.english: I react to this medicine and feel unwell after taking it.

components.note: 西 (west) — traditionally a bird settling on its nest at sunset, hence west; 西 turns up in 要 and 栖.

example.pinyin: Tàiyáng cóng xībiān luòxià.
example.english: The sun sets in the west.
example.fact: 西 is the direction west and also stands for "Western": 西餐 (Western food), 西方 (the West). Surprisingly, 东西 ("east-west") means "stuff, things", read dōngxi, and 西红柿 is the tomato, literally "western red persimmon".

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā zài xuéxiào de xībian.
examples.english: My home is west of the school.

examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng qù Xī'ān lǚyóu.
examples.english: He wants to travel to Xi'an.

components.note: 一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 过, 近, 送: following the edge. The part 力 stands in for 臱 in the traditional 邊.

example.hanzi: 他一边吃饭,一边看手机。
example.pinyin: Tā yìbiān chīfàn, yìbiān kàn shǒujī.
example.english: He eats while looking at his phone.
example.fact: Doubled as "一边...,一边...", it marks two actions happening at the same time ("while...") — a purely grammatical role quite far from its literal meaning "one side," the same kind of drift that turned 一起 (also in this deck) from a literal "rising together" into the abstract "together."

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yìbiān zǒu yìbiān liáo.
examples.english: We chat as we walk.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ zhàn zài lù de yìbiān.
examples.english: Please stand on one side of the road.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — sound and speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问.
斤 (jīn, axe) is only a loose clue for tīng; the traditional 聽 had 耳 ear.
见 (see) — a big eye on a person's legs 儿: a person looking. The same 见 is in 现 appear, 觉 sense, 视 look.

example.pinyin: Wǒ méi tīngjiàn nǐ shuō de huà.
example.english: I didn't hear what you said.
example.fact: 听见 pairs the plain action verb 听 ("to listen") with the result complement 见 ("to succeed in perceiving") — grammatically parallel to 看见 ("to see," literally "look" plus "succeed in perceiving"). Chinese frequently needs an added complement like this to confirm an action actually succeeded, since 听 alone only means "to listen," not that the sound was actually caught.

examples.hanzi: 我听见外面有人在唱歌。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ tīngjiàn wàimiàn yǒu rén zài chànggē.
examples.english: I heard someone singing outside.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ tīngjiàn le ma?
examples.english: Did you hear that?

components.note: 予 (yǔ, give) is only a loose sound hint for shū; compare 序 xù and 预 yù.
月 (moon / flesh) — on the left, likely a squashed 舟 (boat) in 服, not a moon or body part. Dictionary story: a person 卩 putting on a coat 月.
卩 (kneeling person) — on the right, with 又 (hand). The old picture is a hand pressing someone down, 'submit'; clothes (衣服) and service (服务) came later.

example.pinyin: Zhè zhāng chuáng shuì qǐlai hěn shūfu.
example.english: This bed is very comfortable to sleep on.
example.fact: 不舒服 is also the everyday, mild way to say "I feel unwell, under the weather" — a common trap for learners who expect a dedicated word for illness but instead just find the negated form of "comfortable."

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān yǒudiǎn bù shūfu.
examples.english: I don't feel very well today.

examples.pinyin: Zhè bǎ yǐzi zuòzhe hěn shūfu.
examples.english: This chair is comfortable to sit on.

components.note: 夫 (man) — the main part. Dictionary reading: something 丿 slipping from a hand. Memory aid: a man 夫 dropping what he held — 失去 to lose.
攵 (tap, hand with stick) — striking or acting on something: 放, 改, 政, 教; in 败 a blow breaking a cowry 贝 shell (valuable): ruin, defeat.
贝 (bèi) is a loose sound hint for bài.

example.pinyin: Zhè cì kǎoshì tā yòu shībài le.
example.english: He failed this exam again.
example.fact: 失败 pairs two near-synonyms that each independently evoke loss or defeat — 失 ("to lose") and 败 ("to be defeated") — reinforcing each other into one stronger word, the same word-building strategy behind 喜欢 and 应该 from earlier in this deck.

examples.pinyin: Shībài shì chénggōng zhī mǔ.
examples.english: Failure is the mother of success.

examples.pinyin: Zhè cì shíyàn yòu shībài le.
examples.english: The experiment failed again.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 过, 近, 送: a way through.
甬 (yǒng) is a close sound clue for tōng; 甬 also in 痛 tòng, 桶 tǒng and 勇 yǒng.

example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo lù bù tōng.
example.english: This road is blocked.
example.fact: 通 means to pass through or be unobstructed, in 通过 (pass through), 交通 (traffic) and 通知 (notify). As a result complement it means to get something through, as in 想通了 (finally understood). It is also a measure word for calls: 一通电话.

examples.hanzi: 这座桥修好以后，两边就通了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò qiáo xiūhǎo yǐhòu, liǎngbiān jiù tōng le.
examples.english: After the bridge was fixed, both sides were connected.

examples.hanzi: 我给他打了一个电话，但是没打通。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gěi tā dǎ le yí gè diànhuà, dànshì méi dǎtōng.
examples.english: I phoned him but couldn't get through.

components.note: 月 (flesh/meat, not moon here) — oldest form is a hand holding a piece of meat, "to possess"; 月 as meat also appears in 肉 words like 肚 belly and 脑 brain.
日 (sun) — day and time, as in 晴 clear, 早 early, 明 bright; time was read from the sun.
寸 (cùn) stands in for 寺 sì in the traditional 時; sound clue is loose. 寺 also gives 诗 shī and 持 chí.

example.hanzi: 我有时会一个人去看电影。
example.pinyin: Wǒ yǒushí huì yí gè rén qù kàn diànyǐng.
example.english: Sometimes I go watch movies alone.
example.fact: 有时 is a shortened, slightly more literary version of the fuller 有时候 ("there are times when") — both mean "sometimes," but 有时 turns up more in writing, while spoken Mandarin leans toward 有时候 or its close cousin 有的时候.

examples.pinyin: Tā yǒushí qù gōngyuán sànbù.
examples.english: He sometimes takes a walk in the park.

examples.pinyin: Yǒushí xià yǔ, yǒushí chū tàiyáng.
examples.english: Sometimes it rains and sometimes the sun comes out.

components.note: 一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
舟 (boat) — the left part and radical, as in 船 ship. Meaning hint: boats, a tray.
殳 (weapon/tool in hand) — the right part, also in 段 and 投 (throw). Story: handling a tool on a tray to sort things into kinds, hence 'sort, kind'; memory aid only.

example.pinyin: Tā yìbān qī diǎn qǐchuáng.
example.english: He usually gets up at seven.
example.fact: 一般 as an adverb before a verb means "usually, generally" (一般来说, "generally speaking"), while as an adjective before a noun it means "ordinary, so-so" (一般的电影, "a so-so movie") — one word doing two related but distinct grammatical jobs, disambiguated only by its position in the sentence.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā fàndiàn de cài yìbān.
examples.english: The food at this restaurant is so-so.

examples.hanzi: 他们的想法和一般人不一样。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen de xiǎngfǎ hé yìbān rén bù yíyàng.
examples.english: Their thinking is different from ordinary people.

components.note: 虫 (insect, creature) — small animals and insects, as in 蚊 mosquito, 蛇 snake, 虾 shrimp: 蛋 is the egg of a creature.

example.pinyin: Wǒ zǎofàn chī le yí gè jīdàn.
example.english: I had an egg for breakfast.
example.fact: 蛋 mostly appears in compounds: 鸡蛋 (chicken egg), 蛋糕 (cake, "egg cake") and 蛋白 (egg white/protein). It is also an insult word: 笨蛋 (idiot) and 坏蛋 (rascal).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng chī dàngāo.
examples.english: I'd like to eat cake.

examples.pinyin: Zhège dàn diào zài dì shang suì le.
examples.english: This egg fell on the floor and broke.

components.note: 人 (person) — the top. Common reading: a person standing between two sides, a go-between, as in 介绍 to introduce. Early forms may be armour.
八 (eight, divide) — Dictionary: a border dividing people. Memory aid: a person in the middle of two divided parts — in between.
纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord: 红, 线, 组; 绍 first meant to connect, hence to introduce.
召 (zhào) gives a loose sound; same part in 招 zhāo, 照 zhào, 超 chāo.

example.hanzi: 让我介绍一下我的家人。
example.pinyin: Ràng wǒ jièshào yíxià wǒ de jiārén.
example.english: Let me introduce my family.
example.fact: 介绍 nearly always shows up with 一下 tacked on right after it (介绍一下, "let me introduce...") — 一下 softens the request into something casual and brief, the same verb-softening pattern that 一下's own entry in this deck describes.

examples.hanzi: 你能给我介绍一个好医生吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng gěi wǒ jièshào yí ge hǎo yīshēng ma?
examples.english: Can you recommend a good doctor to me?

examples.hanzi: 老师给我们介绍了中国的历史。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī gěi wǒmen jièshàole Zhōngguó de lìshǐ.
examples.english: The teacher introduced us to Chinese history.

components.note: 心 (heart) — mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 意 is what one has in mind.
音 (yīn, sound) is a loose sound clue for yì; 意 itself gives 忆 yì and 亿 yì.
夕 (evening) — the left part, the time-of-day family as in 夜, 多, 梦. Memory aid: things done at night are outside the ordinary.
卜 (divination) — Dictionary story: night 夕 divination 卜, strange and 'outside'. A hedged mnemonic: 外面 outside, 另外 in addition.

example.hanzi: 这次的结果让大家都很意外。
example.pinyin: Zhè cì de jiéguǒ ràng dàjiā dōu hěn yìwài.
example.english: This result surprised everyone.
example.fact: 意外 works as both an adjective ("unexpected, surprising") and a noun ("an accident, a mishap") without changing form — so 出意外 ("something went wrong") uses the noun sense, while 很意外 ("very surprising") uses the adjective sense of the exact same word.

examples.pinyin: Lùshang fāshēngle yí ge yìwài.
examples.english: An accident happened on the road.

examples.pinyin: Zhè ge xiāoxi hěn yìwài.
examples.english: This news is quite unexpected.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 室.
子 (child) — a child in a house: to bear and nurture; characters were later "born" from other characters.

example.pinyin: Nǐ huì xiě zhège zì ma?
example.english: Can you write this character?
example.fact: 字 is a written Chinese character or syllable, such as 汉字, while a "word" in the linguistic sense is 词. A dictionary of characters is a 字典, and 字 was also the formal courtesy name of historical figures, e.g. 诸葛亮, 字孔明.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiě de zì hěn hǎokàn.
examples.english: The characters you write look nice.

examples.pinyin: Zhège zì zěnme dú?
examples.english: How do you read this character?

components.note: 入 (enter) — a pointed shape pushing in; not 人 (person), whose strokes spread outward.

example.pinyin: Qǐng cóng rùkǒu jìnqu.
example.english: Please go in through the entrance.
example.fact: 入 forms 入口 / 出口 (entrance / exit) and verbs such as 加入 (join), 收入 (income) and 入学 (start school). It is also the name of the "entering tone" of Middle Chinese, which Mandarin no longer pronounces as a separate tone.

examples.pinyin: Tā jīnnián gāng rùxué.
examples.english: He just started school this year.

examples.hanzi: 这个公园的入口在哪里？
examples.pinyin: Zhège gōngyuán de rùkǒu zài nǎlǐ?
examples.english: Where is the entrance to this park?

components.note: 贝 (cowry shell, money) — 责 first meant demanding payment of a debt, hence duty. 责 sounds out 债 zhài, 积 jī and 绩 jì.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做; 任 is a duty a person bears.
壬 (rén) gives the same sound, different tone; also in 妊 rèn.

example.hanzi: 照顾孩子是父母的责任。
example.pinyin: Zhàogù háizi shì fùmǔ de zérèn.
example.english: Taking care of children is parents' responsibility.
example.fact: 负责任 ("to bear responsibility, to be responsible") is the verb phrase built on top of the noun 责任 — Chinese frequently turns an abstract noun into an action by adding a light verb like 负 ("to carry, bear") in front of it, rather than switching to a wholly different word the way English distinguishes "responsibility" from "to be responsible."

examples.hanzi: 这是我的责任，我会处理好。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ de zérèn, wǒ huì chǔlǐ hǎo.
examples.english: This is my responsibility, and I'll deal with it.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì nǐ yě yǒu zérèn.
examples.english: You also bear responsibility for this.

components.note: 食 (food, eat) — a lid over a bowl of food. As a left-hand radical it becomes 饣: 饭 meal, 饿 hungry, 饱 full, 饺 dumpling.
牛 (ox) — cattle words like 牧 herd and 特 special; 物 first referred to livestock, then to things in general.
勿 (wù) sounds exactly like 物 — handy for recalling the pronunciation.

example.pinyin: Bīngxiāng lǐ méiyǒu shíwù le.
example.english: There's no food left in the fridge.
example.fact: 食物 is the general, slightly formal word for "food" as a category. Casual speech instead reaches for 东西 (also in this deck) in the fixed phrase 吃东西 ("to eat [something]"), while a specific dish is called 菜 — three overlapping words for eating that aren't freely interchangeable.

examples.pinyin: Xīnxiān de shíwù duì shēntǐ hǎo.
examples.english: Fresh food is good for your body.

examples.hanzi: 我们给小狗买了一些食物。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen gěi xiǎo gǒu mǎile yìxiē shíwù.
examples.english: We bought some food for the puppy.

components.note: 氵 (water radical, 三点水) — water and rivers: 河, 海, 湖; 洛 is the name of a river, now used for sound in foreign names.
各 (gè) gives the sound luò: same part in 路 lù, 落 luò and 络 luò.
木 (tree) — trees and wood: 松, 林, 树; 杉 is a fir tree.
彡 (shān) is the same sound; as a radical 彡 is hair strokes or decoration.
石 (stone) — rocks: 破, 研, 码; 矶 is a rocky reef or jetty.
几 (jī) sounds exactly like 矶; also in 机 jī and 肌 jī.

example.pinyin: Wǒ péngyou zhù zài Luòshānjī.
example.english: My friend lives in Los Angeles.
example.fact: 洛杉矶 is a phonetic transliteration of "Los Angeles," its three characters chosen mainly for sound rather than meaning — 矶 (jī, "a rocky shoal by the water") is a fairly obscure character otherwise, kept alive in everyday use largely because of this one high-frequency city name.

examples.pinyin: Luòshānjī de tiānqì hěn hǎo.
examples.english: The weather in Los Angeles is great.

examples.hanzi: 我们从洛杉矶飞到纽约要五个小时。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen cóng Luòshānjī fēi dào Niǔyuē yào wǔ ge xiǎoshí.
examples.english: Flying from Los Angeles to New York takes five hours.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 遗 is leaving something behind or losing it.
贵 (valuable) — what is precious is what you regret leaving behind or what is left to heirs.
忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings: 怕, 情, 快; 憾 is regret.
感 (gǎn) is a near sound match for hàn; same part in 撼 hàn.

example.hanzi: 没能参加你的婚礼,我很遗憾。
example.pinyin: Méi néng cānjiā nǐ de hūnlǐ, wǒ hěn yíhàn.
example.english: I regret not being able to attend your wedding.
example.fact: 遗憾 describes regret over something outside one's control — a missed opportunity, bad luck, someone else's loss — while 后悔 is reserved for regretting one's own choice or action. English "regret" blurs the two together, but mixing them up is a common tell of a learner.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì ràng wǒ hěn yíhàn.
examples.english: This matter makes me feel very sorry.

examples.hanzi: 最大的遗憾是没有早点学外语。
examples.pinyin: Zuì dà de yíhàn shì méiyǒu zǎodiǎn xué wàiyǔ.
examples.english: My biggest regret is not studying a foreign language earlier.

meanings: to come over from the enemy's side

components.note: 又 (hand) — a hand pushing against a cliff 厂: turning back, opposite. Sound series: 饭 fàn, 板 bǎn, 版 bǎn, 返 fǎn.
止 (foot) — a foot heading straight for a target line: upright, correct. 正 gives sound to 证 zhèng, 整 zhěng and 政 zhèng.

example.hanzi: 算了吧,反正你说了他也不会听。
example.pinyin: Suànle ba, fǎnzhèng nǐ shuō le tā yě bú huì tīng.
example.english: Forget it — he won't listen anyway even if you say something.
example.fact: Beyond its everyday sense of "anyway, regardless," dictionaries also carry an older, specialized meaning for 反正 — "to defect, to come over to the correct/legitimate side" — a more literal reading of its two characters (反 "to turn against" + 正 "correct, legitimate") that survives from a more formal historical and political register.

examples.hanzi: 反正我今天没事，我陪你去吧。
examples.pinyin: Fǎnzhèng wǒ jīntiān méi shì, wǒ péi nǐ qù ba.
examples.english: I'm free today anyway, so I'll go with you.

examples.hanzi: 不管怎么样，反正我不去。
examples.pinyin: Bùguǎn zěnmeyàng, fǎnzhèng wǒ bú qù.
examples.english: Whatever happens, I'm not going anyway.

components.note: 乂 (to cut, crisscross) — old for mowing or cutting. Dictionary story: someone cut down 乂 and buried in a wooden coffin 木, a vivid memory aid.
木 (tree, wood) — the bottom. In 杀 it is a leftover of the old 殺 form rather than meaning wood; 殺 also had 殳 (weapon in hand).
手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.

example.hanzi: 电影里的杀手最后被警察抓住了。
example.pinyin: Diànyǐng lǐ de shāshǒu zuìhòu bèi jǐngchá zhuāzhù le.
example.english: The killer in the movie was finally caught by the police.
example.fact: 杀手 also extends into a common, casual metaphor for anything that "kills" something non-literally — 时间杀手 ("a time-killer," something that eats up huge amounts of time) is a frequent coinage built the same way English calls an addictive game or show "a real time-killer."

examples.hanzi: 小说里的杀手是个神秘的人。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎoshuō lǐ de shāshǒu shì ge shénmì de rén.
examples.english: The killer in the novel is a mysterious person.

examples.hanzi: 警察终于抓住了那个杀手。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá zhōngyú zhuāzhùle nà ge shāshǒu.
examples.english: The police finally caught the killer.

components.note: 讠 (speech, simplified 言) — speech and talking: 说, 计, 谈; 设 is to set up or plan by instruction.
殳 (shū, hand holding a tool) is only a loose sound clue; also in 投 tóu and 股 gǔ.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; counting aloud.
十 (ten) — counting up to ten: 计 is to count and reckon.

example.hanzi: 这个网站是我朋友设计的。
example.pinyin: Zhège wǎngzhàn shì wǒ péngyou shèjì de.
example.english: This website was designed by my friend.
example.fact: 设计 functions as both verb and noun without changing form, joining a long list of Chinese words with this flexibility already seen in this deck (工作, 意外) — English marks the difference between "to design" and "a design," while Chinese relies entirely on sentence position.

examples.pinyin: Tā zài yì jiā gōngsī zuò shèjì.
examples.english: She works in design at a company.

examples.hanzi: 我想设计一个新的房间。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng shèjì yí ge xīn de fángjiān.
examples.english: I want to design a new room.

components.note: 寸 (hand, inch) — a hand, as in 对, 寻, 守; with 圭 (a heap of earth) it means heaping earth to mark a border, then to seal.

example.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān xiě le yì fēng xìn.
example.english: I wrote a letter yesterday.
example.fact: 封 is a measure word for letters and emails (一封信, 一封邮件). It also means to seal or close off: 封面 (cover), 封锁 (blockade), 封城 (lock down a city), and 封建 (feudal) comes from the old sense of granting land.

examples.hanzi: 他每个月给妈妈寄一封信。
examples.pinyin: Tā měi gè yuè gěi māma jì yì fēng xìn.
examples.english: Every month he sends his mom a letter.

examples.pinyin: Dàxuě bǎ lù fēng zhù le.
examples.english: The heavy snow has blocked the road.

components.note: 贝 (cowry shell, money) — wealth and trade: 财, 费, 买, 货; 赢 is to win or gain a profit.
彳 (step) — walking and going, as in 行, 往, 很 very.
寸 (hand) — oldest form is a hand grabbing a cowrie shell (money): 得 is "to obtain". The shell has worn down to 旦.

example.pinyin: Zhège qiúduì yíngdé le guànjūn.
example.english: This team won the championship.
example.fact: 赢得 is a more formal, written-register pairing than the plain verb 赢 alone — 赢 by itself already means "to win" and can stand alone in speech (赢了! "Won!"), while 赢得 almost always needs a following object (赢得冠军, 赢得尊重) and reads noticeably more like news writing than casual talk.

examples.pinyin: Tā yíngdéle dàjiā de zūnzhòng.
examples.english: He earned everyone's respect.

examples.hanzi: 我们很想赢得这场比赛。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen hěn xiǎng yíngdé zhè chǎng bǐsài.
examples.english: We really want to win this match.

components.note: 止 (foot) — a foot heading straight for a target line: upright, correct. 正 gives sound to 证 zhèng, 整 zhěng and 政 zhèng.
日 (sun) — on top; the usual explanation is sun over 正 "straight, correct": what is clear and straight is "right, is". A memory aid, not firm etymology.

example.pinyin: Zhè zhèngshì wǒ xiǎng yào de dá'àn.
example.english: This is exactly the answer I wanted.
example.fact: 正是 intensifies the plain copula 是 ("to be") with 正 ("precisely, exactly right") in front of it — functioning much like 就是 (also in this deck) as an emphatic "is exactly." 正 and 就 work as near-interchangeable intensifiers Mandarin uses constantly to sharpen an otherwise plain statement of identity.

examples.pinyin: Zhè zhèng shì wǒmen xūyào de.
examples.english: This is exactly what we need.

examples.hanzi: 现在正是春天，花开得很美。
examples.pinyin: Xiànzài zhèng shì chūntiān, huā kāi de hěn měi.
examples.english: It is just spring now and the flowers are blooming beautifully.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢: to prove by saying.
正 (zhèng) gives the exact sound; 正 also in 整 zhěng and 政 zhèng.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 警察正在寻找目击证人。
example.pinyin: Jǐngchá zhèngzài xúnzhǎo mùjī zhèngrén.
example.english: The police are looking for eyewitnesses.
example.fact: 证人 is built from 证 ("to prove, evidence") plus 人 ("person") — literally "a proof-person." It's the same logical pattern behind many Chinese role nouns that fuse a function directly onto 人, like 主人 ("host/owner," literally "master-person") or 客人 ("guest," literally "guest-person").

examples.pinyin: Tā shì zhè qǐ shìgù de zhèngrén.
examples.english: He is a witness of this accident.

examples.hanzi: 法官请证人说出看到的情况。
examples.pinyin: Fǎguān qǐng zhèngrén shuōchū kàndào de qíngkuàng.
examples.english: The judge asked the witness to describe what was seen.

components.note: 羊 (sheep) — traditionally 羊 over 大: a big, fat sheep was good, tasty and pleasing, hence beautiful. 羊 also appears in 样 and 洋.
丽 (beautiful) — simplified 麗, which showed a deer 鹿 with antlers, a symbol of grace. Seen in 美丽.

example.pinyin: Zhè shì yí zuò měilì de chéngshì.
example.english: This is a beautiful city.
example.fact: 美丽 leans literary and is mainly reserved for describing scenery, cities, or a formal kind of beauty — for everyday, all-purpose "pretty, good-looking," spoken Mandarin overwhelmingly prefers the shorter, more casual 好看 or 漂亮 instead.

examples.pinyin: Tā de gēshēng hěn měilì.
examples.english: Her singing voice is beautiful.

examples.hanzi: 这个美丽的故事让我很感动。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge měilì de gùshi ràng wǒ hěn gǎndòng.
examples.english: This beautiful story moved me deeply.

components.note: 土 (earth) — soil and land: 地, 场, 坏; 压 is earth pressed down under a cliff 厂.
力 (strength) — an old picture of an arm or a plough, a tool of effort. As a radical it marks strength: 办, 助, 动, 努, 男.

example.hanzi: 工作压力太大,他每天都很累。
example.pinyin: Gōngzuò yālì tài dà, tā měitiān dōu hěn lèi.
example.english: Work pressure is too much; he's tired every day.
example.fact: 压力 covers both literal physical pressure (as in physics or engineering) and figurative psychological stress with the same word — 有压力 ("to be under pressure, stressed") is one of the most common ways Chinese speakers today describe work or study-related stress.

examples.pinyin: Kǎoshì qián, wǒ de yālì hěn dà.
examples.english: I'm under a lot of pressure before exams.

examples.pinyin: Yùndòng kěyǐ jiǎnshǎo yālì.
examples.english: Exercise can reduce stress.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — tasting and speaking: 吃, 喝, 嗅; 味 is flavor.
未 (wèi) sounds exactly like 味; also 妹 mèi.
辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 这 this, 过 pass, 近 near; a 道 is a road, then a way or principle.
首 (shǒu, head) is only a loose sound hint for dào; 首 also means "head/first", fitting a lead-the-way road.

example.pinyin: Zhège tāng de wèidao hěn hǎo.
example.english: This soup tastes great.
example.fact: 味道 extends past literal taste into a figurative "sense, feel, vibe" of a situation — 有点味道 can describe an interesting or nuanced quality in music, writing, or a place, much like English stretches "flavor" beyond food ("a certain flavor to the writing").

examples.pinyin: Zhè ge cài de wèidao yǒudiǎn xián.
examples.english: This dish tastes a bit salty.

examples.hanzi: 屋子里有一股奇怪的味道。
examples.pinyin: Wūzi lǐ yǒu yì gǔ qíguài de wèidao.
examples.english: There is a strange smell in the room.

components.note: 氵 (water radical, 三点水) — water: 河, 海, 汤; 淘 is to rinse and sift in water.
匋 (táo) sounds exactly like 淘; same part in 陶 táo and 萄 táo.
氵 (water radical, 三点水) — water: 河, 海, 汤; 汰 is to rinse away what is useless.
太 (tài) sounds exactly like 汰; also in 态 tài.

example.hanzi: 他在第一轮比赛就被淘汰了。
example.pinyin: Tā zài dì yī lún bǐsài jiù bèi táotài le.
example.english: He was eliminated in the very first round of the competition.
example.fact: 淘汰 combines two water-related verbs — 淘 ("to wash, to rinse," as in panning for gold) and 汰 ("to rinse away, to wash out") — into a vivid image of impurities being washed out, which is exactly how it's used today for eliminating a weaker competitor, product, or outdated technology.

examples.hanzi: 这种旧手机已经被淘汰了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng jiù shǒujī yǐjīng bèi táotài le.
examples.english: This kind of old phone has been phased out.

examples.hanzi: 不努力的人会被社会淘汰。
examples.pinyin: Bù nǔlì de rén huì bèi shèhuì táotài.
examples.english: People who don't work hard get left behind by society.

components.note: 厂 (cliff) — stone and cliffs: 厚 thick, 原 origin, 压 press; 厉 first meant a whetstone, hence sharp and severe.
害 (hài) is a loose sound clue for 割 gē and 辖 xiá; as a word it means to harm, as in 厉害.

example.pinyin: Nǐ de Zhōngwén shuō de zhēn lìhai!
example.english: Your Chinese is really amazing!
example.fact: 厉害 swings between two very different registers depending on context — as praise it means "amazing, impressive" (你真厉害, "you're awesome"), but attached to pain, weather, or an illness it means "severe, intense" (疼得很厉害, "hurts a lot") — the same word covering both a compliment and a complaint.

examples.hanzi: 这个孩子真厉害，才五岁就会游泳了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge háizi zhēn lìhai, cái wǔ suì jiù huì yóuyǒng le.
examples.english: This kid is amazing, swimming at only five.

examples.pinyin: Tā tóutòng de hěn lìhai.
examples.english: His headache is severe.

components.note: 鱼 (fish) — a picture of a fish: head on top, scaly body 田, tail 一. As a radical (鱼) it marks fish, as in 鲨, 鲜.

example.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan chī yú.
example.english: I like eating fish.
example.fact: 鱼 counts with 条 (一条鱼). It is part of New Year symbolism because 鱼 (yú) sounds like 余 (surplus), so serving fish brings the wish 年年有余, "may there be surplus every year".

examples.pinyin: Jīnwǎn wǒmen chī hóngshāo yú.
examples.english: Tonight we're having braised fish.

examples.pinyin: Hé lǐ yǒu hěn duō xiǎoyú.
examples.english: There are many small fish in the river.

components.note: 身 (body, bow) — 身 is a worn-down picture of a bow, with a hand 寸 drawing it — 射 is to shoot.

example.pinyin: Tā shèzhòng le mùbiāo.
example.english: He hit the target.
example.fact: 射 is to shoot an arrow or emit something: 发射 (launch), 射击 (shoot), 照射 (shine on) and 反射 (reflect). In football 射门 means to shoot at goal.

examples.pinyin: Dìdi yòng shuǐqiāng shè wǒ.
examples.english: My younger brother squirts me with a water gun.

examples.pinyin: Tàiyáng de guāng shè jìn le fángjiān.
examples.english: The sunlight shone into the room.
